title: Vela
summary: An e-bike launch told through scroll-driven assembly, a city ride, and a 3D configurator.
overview: A launch microsite for a fictional e-bike, designed to let the product tell its own story. Seven chapters move from a bold opening to assembly, a turntable, a city ride, specifications, colourways, and a test-ride invitation. The supporting pages turn that story into something visitors can explore and configure.
highlights: A shared scene engine maps scroll progress to image sequences, video, and product callouts, loading the next scene progressively.
A Three.js configurator changes colour, rack, and basket options, with image sharing and a lighter model for smaller devices.
A complete static reading mode supports reduced motion and low-memory devices; booking routes handle shops, time slots, and confirmations.
note: Concept project. Product specifications, shops, and imagery are fictional or procedurally generated. Real confirmation-email delivery requires service configuration.
alt: Vela e-bike configurator with a procedural bicycle model and colour options

title: Orbit
summary: A modular product story with colour selection, sound demos, and a layout-aware CMS studio.
overview: Orbit is a fictional smart-speaker family presented through a responsive bento grid. Tile sizes establish a clear hierarchy, while product details, sound samples, and colour choices make the grid an interface rather than just a layout. Orbit Mini shares the same engine with its own composition.
highlights: Five tile sizes and a dense CSS grid are checked against a placement model to prevent holes and preserve reading order.
Colour choices stay synchronized across the hero, product links, and buy bar, and can be shared through the URL.
A file-backed CMS studio supports tile ordering, per-breakpoint sizing, draft previews, and validated publishing.
note: Concept project. Orbit and its retailers are fictional. The checkout is a demonstration handoff, and the CMS studio is not production-authenticated.
alt: Orbit product website with a dark smart-speaker hero and modular feature tiles

title: Synapse
summary: A dark, developer-first API website with interactive pricing, model discovery, and searchable docs.
overview: A fictional AI inference platform with a near-black canvas and restrained violet-to-cyan accents. The interface brings working code examples, model comparisons, and understandable pricing to the foreground, instead of relying on a visual effect alone.
highlights: Copyable examples in four languages use build-time syntax highlighting, with the selected language shared across pages.
A single pricing dataset powers the model catalogue, pricing table, and URL-shareable cost calculator.
MDX documentation is indexed for keyboard-driven search; the demo signup generates a clearly fake API key.
note: Concept project. Models, latency figures, SDK names, and API keys are simulated; no real inference service or account is created.
alt: Synapse dark API landing page with a violet headline and terminal example

title: Stackd
summary: Freelancer invoicing with thick outlines, bright colour, and a live invoice-building demo.
overview: A marketing website for a fictional invoicing tool, built around hard shadows, expressive typography, and bold flat colour. Beneath the visual personality is a practical product journey: explore features, build a sample invoice, compare plans, and read release notes.
highlights: The interactive invoice preview responds to client, amount, currency, description, and due-date inputs without storing them.
Billing and currency controls share one pricing model, with shareable state and region-aware defaults.
A static Next.js export includes Markdown release notes, an RSS feed, responsive component states, and a pausable integration marquee.
note: Concept project. Signup and login point to reserved example domains. The invoice demo does not send invoices or process payments.
alt: Stackd invoicing website with chunky black outlines, yellow accents, and an invoice dashboard

title: Atelier Nord
summary: A bilingual architecture portfolio where a disciplined grid lets the work speak for itself.
overview: A portfolio for a fictional Copenhagen architecture studio, using generous white space, a twelve-column grid, and a tightly controlled palette. The content system supports complete English and Danish versions of every project, with art-directed images and clear project facts.
highlights: Markdown content collections drive the project index, sector filters, and full- and half-width image layouts.
The gallery offers grid and table views, a keyboard-accessible lightbox, and previous/next navigation that respects the active filter.
Localized routes preserve context between Danish and English; the enquiry form has server validation and a no-JavaScript submission path.
note: Concept project. The studio, architecture projects, people, and generated imagery are fictional. Live email delivery needs an email-service configuration.
alt: Atelier Nord minimalist architecture portfolio with oversized typography and architectural imagery

title: Lumen
summary: A calm budgeting experience with translucent surfaces and an interactive, three-persona dashboard.
overview: A fictional budgeting app presented through translucent panels and soft colour fields. The design balances glassmorphism with legible financial information, carrying the same visual system from the landing page into a hands-on dashboard preview.
highlights: Three bundled personas switch balances, transactions, budgets, and savings goals without a network request.
Native budget sliders update spending totals; SVG charts include text summaries and hidden data tables.
A contrast-checking build gate covers overlapping backgrounds, with solid-panel and increased-contrast fallbacks.
note: Concept project with sample financial data. Bank connections, regulatory references, and app-store destinations are placeholders, not a live financial service.
alt: Lumen budgeting landing page with translucent financial cards over pastel colour fields

title: Wildroot
summary: Hand-drawn warmth meets a practical bakery pre-order, collection, and workshop-booking flow.
overview: A fictional sourdough bakery and café with a welcoming, organic identity. Illustrated marks, irregular image masks, and handwritten notes sit above a working pre-order-for-collection app, with a separate phone-friendly workflow for bakery staff.
highlights: Customers choose a shop, collection date, time slot, and products, with allergen filtering and an order cut-off.
Stock and workshop seats are reserved under per-key locks; a declined simulated payment releases the reservation.
Staff tools manage bake quantities, collections, daily specials, and closures, alongside a reusable thirty-illustration SVG set.
note: Concept project. Payments and notifications are simulated, the staff area has no authentication, and in-memory demo data resets with the server.
alt: Wildroot bakery website with illustrated sourdough loaves, organic shapes, and handwritten accents

title: Doodle Math
summary: A playful maths world with clay mascots, adaptive questions, and a thoughtful grown-up experience.
overview: A marketing site and playable demo for a fictional maths app for ages five to eleven. Puffy clay surfaces and four generated mascots create the child-facing identity, while the parent and school journeys use clear pricing, curriculum information, and safety explanations.
highlights: An eight-question demo adapts difficulty to answers and supports touch, mouse, and keyboard without saving child data.
A grown-up gate separates the game from adult routes, with narration controls and reduced-motion alternatives.
A curriculum explorer, family/school pricing, trial forms, and demo bookings share tested logic; first-party metrics avoid tracking identifiers.
note: Concept project. Characters are procedurally rendered and narration is placeholder audio. The app and its family testimonials are fictional.
alt: Doodle Math learning website with pastel clay characters and a large playful maths headline

title: The Long Field
summary: A reader-funded magazine prototype built around expressive type and art-directed long-form stories.
overview: A fictional food and farming magazine with the rhythm of a printed publication. Serif headlines, ruled columns, drop caps, pull quotes, and sidenotes bring editorial structure to a plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript implementation.
highlights: Structured story blocks support feature articles, short reads, photo essays, sidebars, and galleries.
Five opening templates and four tones give each story its own art direction, with responsive editor previews.
Issue archives, contributor pages, filtered search, reading metering, and speech-synthesis narration complete the prototype.
note: Front-end concept. Membership, payment, and metering are local simulations; illustrations are generated SVG plates, not commissioned photography.
alt: The Long Field editorial magazine cover with serif typography, columns, and illustrated stories

title: PULSE 27
summary: A type-led festival website with a personal schedule, clash detection, and an offline-ready programme.
overview: A fictional three-day festival website where variable typography becomes the main visual. Oversized lettering and day-specific palettes set the energy, while schedule planning, ticket information, and a calm mode keep the experience useful.
highlights: A fit-text system accounts for variable-font width and weight, keeping reactive headlines within their containers.
Visitors can save sets to My PULSE, see schedule clashes, and export their choices to a calendar.
A service worker caches the programme for offline use; a lightweight queue page and visible-only ticket polling support the ticket journey.
note: Concept project. Festival details, artists, and ticket availability are demo content. Large-scale queue load testing is not claimed.
alt: PULSE 27 festival website dominated by large variable lettering and acid-colour accents

title: Loud House
summary: A gallery identity turned up to full volume, with exhibition discovery, ticket booking, and calm mode.
overview: A fictional east-London art gallery and its MORE exhibition microsite. Clashing patterns, collage, mixed typefaces, and saturated colour make the creative identity unmistakable, while quieter information panels keep visit planning clear.
highlights: Exhibition and event pages use shared content structures and reusable art, collage, sticker, and information-panel components.
A multi-step booking flow covers dates, entry slots, ticket quantities, visitor details, and a demo confirmation with a QR code.
A persistent calm mode removes patterns, collage, and movement; visitor resources include sensory information and a large-print route.
note: Concept project. The gallery, artists, exhibitions, memberships, and ticketing data are fictional demonstrations rather than a live venue service.
alt: Loud House gallery website with layered oversized typography, collage, and vivid pink and yellow

title: Thermo
summary: Tactile smart-home controls with accessible dials, room schedules, and real-time device-state sync.
overview: A fictional smart-home hub with a soft-UI product website and a connected dashboard. The project explores how raised and recessed surfaces can feel tactile without making controls dependent on low-contrast shadows.
highlights: A circular temperature dial supports dragging, buttons, and a complete keyboard interaction model.
A simulated WebSocket hub synchronizes screens, with optimistic updates, rejected-command rollback, and offline state feedback.
Room schedules include non-drag controls; high-contrast and wall-tablet modes adapt the same shared component library.
note: Concept project with a simulated hub, not real Matter-device integration. Real-device kiosk testing and usability studies are not claimed.
alt: Thermo smart-home website with soft raised controls and a circular temperature dial

title: Static FM
summary: An early-web radio desktop with a persistent player, draggable windows, and a modern accessible shell.
overview: A fictional independent radio station presented as a playful early-2000s desktop. Bevelled windows, pixel details, and a Winamp-inspired player hide a responsive application with shareable routes, persistent playback, and a conventional simple mode.
highlights: One audio player persists across navigation and supports Media Session metadata, archive playback, and a Web Audio visualiser.
URL-driven windows can be opened, focused, dragged, minimized, and maximized; tablet and phone layouts use dedicated shells.
A time-zone-aware programme supports calendar export and offline access, alongside switchable skins and reduced-motion controls.
note: Concept project. The default stream is a synthesized demo loop, listener counts are simulated, and guestbook moderation is local. Real membership needs a backend.
alt: Static FM retro desktop with bevelled application windows and a radio player
